text: Lesson 18 covered feeds as a stream of IOCs, but not how those IOCs get described so every organization's tools can read them the same way. Today we'll cover STIX and TAXII — the real industry-standard pairing for describing and physically exchanging threat intelligence between organizations.

STIX, Structured Threat Information eXpression, is a standardized, OASIS-maintained JSON-based language for describing threat intelligence in detail. It doesn't just hold a bare IP address — it can describe a whole threat actor, a campaign, the specific indicators tied to it, and the relationships connecting all of them, so the data means the exact same thing no matter whose tools it lands in.

TAXII, Trusted Automated eXchange of Indicator Information, defines how that STIX data physically moves between organizations. It's an HTTPS-based API specification: a TAXII server hosts one or more collections of STIX data on a given topic, and a TAXII client at another organization connects in to pull new content, or subscribes to a channel to receive it the moment it's published. STIX is the what, TAXII is the how.

Almost no one uses STIX without TAXII, or the reverse — they were designed as a pair specifically to solve threat-intel sharing, and that pairing is the real industry standard today for automated, machine-to-machine exchange. CISA's Automated Indicator Sharing program and open-source platforms like MISP, widely used by ISACs, both support STIX and TAXII for exactly this reason.

Picture two ISAC member companies hit by the same attack campaign days apart. Company A packages the malicious IPs, hashes, and phishing pattern into a STIX bundle and publishes it to the ISAC's TAXII server. Company B's TIP, already subscribed, pulls that bundle within minutes, and its firewall updates automatically before its own analysts finish investigating.

That's STIX and TAXII working together — one organization's discovery becoming every subscriber's defense, automatically. Next up, Lesson 20 looks at OSINT: using publicly available information defensively, to understand your own exposed attack surface before an attacker does.
